findings.element: Overlay exit paths — close (top left), Cancel (footer), and the Escape key
findings.finding: All three exit paths silently discard the entire configuration with no unsaved-changes prompt, and Escape is bound unconditionally at the document level rather than to the overlay.
findings.user_impact: A user who has built a full rule across three sections loses all of it to one stray Escape or one mis-aimed close and has to rebuild from scratch, with no undo and no indication that anything was lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Track a dirty flag from the moment cfg diverges from saved and route close, Cancel and Escape through a Discard your changes? confirmation, ignoring Escape when it is dismissing an open select rather than the overlay.

evidence.action: Edited values in the overlay (scope toggles, source select, days field), then closed it with Cancel, with the close button, and with Escape; reopened via Edit rule
evidence.observed: Every path closed immediately with no prompt and no toast; the reopened overlay showed the previous saved values, so all edits were gone. The handler is a document-level keydown with no dirty check and no target check, and closeOverlay only removes a class - cfg is re-cloned from saved on the next open.

findings.element: Default-matcher reference card (What Synder does today, by default) and the state revealed when the master switch is turned on
findings.finding: The card promises Nothing is pre-filled, but switching the master switch on reveals a complete pre-built rule — all three scope rows on, 90 days, and a condition row the user never authored — with Save already enabled.
findings.user_impact: Users told to expect a blank canvas instead face a populated rule they will reasonably read as Synder recommendation, and can save a matching rule containing a Memo on statement condition they never chose, which silently narrows matching so that invoices with an empty memo stop matching at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Either start section 2 with no condition rows and the scope rows genuinely unset, or drop the Nothing is pre-filled sentence and label the revealed values explicitly as a starting point the user is expected to review before saving.

evidence.action: Read the reference card with the master switch off, then switched it on and inspected sections 1 and 2 and the footer before touching any control
evidence.observed: Card text reads You are about to replace exactly this. Nothing is pre-filled, so no existing configuration changes until you build a rule and save it. On switching on, section 1 showed all three rows on with 90 days and invoice_number/is equal to, and section 2 showed one pre-seeded row - payment invoice note is equal to the invoice Memo on statement. validate() returned no errors, so Save was enabled.

findings.element: Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment — the GSP settings row and the identical toggle in section 3
findings.finding: The same setting, explicitly labelled one value, two places, uses two different commit models: on the GSP row it saves the instant it is flipped, while inside the overlay it is a draft edit that only lands on Save and is thrown away by Cancel, close or Escape.
findings.user_impact: This toggle is the entire answer to what happens when nothing is found, so a user who opens the rule specifically to flip it and then closes the overlay without pressing Save - having changed nothing else and been told it is one shared value - leaves believing the no-match behaviour changed when it did not.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the overlay copy of this row behave identically to the GSP row by committing on flip, or drop it from the overlay and show it there as read-only reference text with a link back to the setting that owns it.

evidence.action: Flipped the toggle on the GSP row and observed the result, then reopened the overlay, flipped the same toggle in section 3, and closed with Cancel; reopened to inspect the value
evidence.observed: The GSP flip persisted with no Save step (it writes saved.cancelSync and cfg.cancelSync directly, then re-renders). The section 3 flip only wrote the draft; after Cancel the value reverted, because openOverlay re-clones cfg from saved and only Save copies cfg back. Both rows meanwhile assert One value - changing it in either place changes both.

findings.element: Section 1, are dated within N days either side of the payment — the row toggle when the no-date-limit admin flag is off
findings.finding: This toggle renders at full opacity and is visually identical to the two live toggles above and below it, but clicking it does nothing at all - no state change, no message, no acknowledgement - and the screen renders its own unavailable states two different ways.
findings.user_impact: Users click a control that looks exactly as interactive as its neighbours, get zero response, and cannot tell whether the product is broken or the setting is restricted, with no action available to request the unlock even once they read the hint.
findings.suggested_fix: Render this toggle in the same visibly disabled treatment already used for the plan-gated master switch, and on click surface the reason with an actionable next step instead of returning silently.

evidence.action: With the admin no-limit flag off, clicked the date row toggle repeatedly, then compared its rendering with the plan-gated master-switch toggle; re-tested with the admin flag on
evidence.observed: State stayed on with no visible feedback of any kind; the handler returns early. The wrapper gets .tog.nolock which sets only cursor:not-allowed, whereas the plan-gated toggle gets .tog.dis which sets cursor:not-allowed and opacity .5 - so on the same screen one blocked toggle is dimmed and this one is not. With the admin flag on, the identical click switched the row off and revealed the No date limit warning.

gaps: Escape while a native select is open was never exercised. The overlay is built almost entirely from native selects and the Escape handler is registered on document with no target or defaultPrevented check, so dismissing a dropdown with Escape may close the whole overlay and discard the rule - a much more frequent trigger for UX-1 than a deliberate Escape, but unverified.

The plan gate was only observed from the GSP side, where Configure is disabled. The overlay own Starter error block and its Available on Pro and above footer are therefore unreachable by a real Starter user.
The generic-customer warning is not recorded in the state map controls, so whether it appears at the right moment and whether it should block rather than warn is unverified.
No loading, latency or save-failure state exists or was exercised - Save is synchronous in the prototype.

Save was only exercised from a valid state. Whether the disabled Save plus the count-only footer message lets a user locate an error in a long scrolling overlay was not tested, and no jump-to-error affordance exists.
